title: About this course: Introduction to C++ for DSA
overview: This course moves a C programmer into C++ so that data-structure and algorithm work becomes easier. It covers C++ input/output, dynamic memory, classes and objects, the `string` class, sorting with `sort()` and custom comparators, and arrays of objects. The module pages that follow show every program with a real run and a plain-words walkthrough.

concepts.explain: Most C ideas (variables, loops, arrays, pointers) still work. C++ adds friendlier tools: `cin`/`cout`, `string`, classes and the STL algorithms.

concepts.term: Commented code as a study aid
concepts.explain: Many files in this course carry long beginner-friendly comments that explain why each formatter or function is used. Read the comment and the line together when revising.

Module 1 (I/O, switch, min/max) -> Module 2 (heap memory) -> Module 3 (classes, constructors, `this`, `sort`) -> Mid-term -> Modules 5-6 (strings, stringstream) -> Module 7 (array of objects, comparators) -> Final exam.

recap: C++ keeps C's core and adds safer, shorter tools for DSA.
Heap memory (`new`/`delete`) outlives a function; stack memory does not.
`string`, `stringstream` and `sort()` save a lot of manual work.
Custom comparators let you sort objects by any rule you need.

check_yourself.q: Why do DSA courses usually prefer C++ over C?
check_yourself.a: C++ has the STL (`sort`, `string`, containers) and cleaner I/O, so you write less boilerplate and focus on the algorithm.

check_yourself.q: What is the main difference between a stack variable and a heap variable?
check_yourself.a: A stack variable dies when its function returns; a heap variable (made with `new`) lives until you `delete` it.
